label: Multi language code extractor uses pluggable backend registry with web tree sitter pinned to 0.20.8 for grammar ABI match evidence chunk 1
title: Multi language code extractor uses pluggable backend registry with web tree sitter pinned to 0.20.8 for grammar ABI match evidence chunk 1
summary: Phase-1b made lib/code-extract pluggable: backends/registry.js dispatches extractFile(relPath, source, ext) -> {symbols, edges} by extension. JS/TS/JSX -> backends/babel.js (wraps the unchanged parse.js+symbols.js, so the Phase-1 test passes verbatim, 35/35). Python/Go/Rust/Java/C/C++ -> backends/treesitter.js via web-tree-sitter (WASM) with .wasm grammars VENDORED under lib/code-extract/grammars/ (published via the package files:[lib/] entry; node_modules is gitignored so vendoring is how grammars ship). extractRepo stays the SYNC public entry and now walks the UNION of all backend extensions; extractRepoAsync (or awaiting initTreeSitter() once) boots the WASM runtime before sync extract — babel needs no init so the JS/TS path is unchanged/synchronous. A tree-sitter file reached before init is counted parse_failed, never silently empty.
